rationale: The golden reference submission, which correctly implements the pinned interface and timing contract, is rejected by evaluate.py on FR1, FR3, and FR4 with the diagnostic 'missing PROBE for cycle 0' / 'missing PROBE for collision cycle 0'. This is a validation_report issue == 'golden_rejected' scenario. The golden's own metrics (cycle_accurate_match_rate=0.995) show its simulated behavior is correct, and the failure is a probe/stimulus indexing bug inside evaluation/tb_regfile.v or evaluate.py's parsing of the testbench output, not a genuine behavioral defect in the golden. The analyzer confirms the documented fix (merging load/drive into one initial block) did not actually eliminate the cycle-0 probe loss, and retries reproduced the identical deterministic failure signature. Because the golden fails, mutation_status is blocked_by_differential, mutation_score is not meaningful (0.0), and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0 despite full requirement mapping coverage. This benchmark case cannot be shipped until the harness correctly accepts the golden.
revision_instructions: evaluate.py (and/or evaluation/tb_regfile.v) must be fixed so the probe capturing cycle-0 (and the collision-cycle-0 probe) is never dropped, for FR1, FR3, and FR4. Concretely: (1) the testbench's stimulus-application and probe-sampling logic must both live in a single, correctly-ordered initial block (or equivalent deterministic scheduling) so that the very first write-then-read cycle and the very first same-cycle collision event are captured and recorded before any downstream check consumes them off by one index; (2) verify the probe array/list used by the FR1/FR3/FR4 checkers is populated starting at index 0 and that evaluate.py's requirement-checking code reads from that same starting index — do not let the checker assume a probe exists for cycle 0 while the testbench only starts recording from cycle 1 (or vice versa); (3) grade FR1/FR3/FR4 purely behaviorally by comparing the submission's simulated rdata0/rdata1 waveform against a reference waveform derived from the pinned public_spec.interface timing contract, sampled at every defined probe point including cycle 0 and the collision cycle 0 -- do not skip or special-case the first cycle; (4) after the fix, rerun the differential validation and confirm the golden submission (which correctly implements zero-latency combinational reads with natural write-forwarding per the pinned interface) passes all FR and SR checks with exit code 0, while the naive-stub and the intentionally-flawed baselines (extra read latency, stale collision value, no reset clear) each still fail the corresponding checks; (5) add a lightweight regression assertion in the harness itself that runs against a correct implementation and requires all [TEST] PASS / exit 0 before the case can be considered valid, so this probe-loss bug cannot silently reappear. Do not weaken FR1/FR3/FR4 to pass by matching source text or baseline-specific structure -- continue judging strictly on simulated I/O behavior at the pinned ports.
